title: Handmade Paper Craft Training for Women
summary: Enable economic independence for women from underserved communities through skill building and income generation.
description:
Kaagaz Sakhi is a women employability initiative aimed at empowering women from economically weaker households by nurturing skills, confidence, and sustainable livelihood opportunities. Rooted in the traditional art of handmade paper crafting—an artisanal heritage for which Kalpi holds a prestigious GI tag—the project combines cultural preservation with economic independence.

Through this initiative, 50 women are currently undergoing structured, hands-on training in handmade paper craft techniques, along with foundational learning in numerical literacy and basic marketing skills. The holistic approach enables participants not only to master the craft but also to understand pricing, sales, and pathways to income generation.

By fostering self-reliance and entrepreneurship, Kaagaz Sakhi helps women take meaningful steps toward financial independence while keeping a rich local art form alive. The project reflects a deep commitment to creating dignified livelihoods, strengthening communities, and ensuring that traditional skills continue to thrive across generations.
